title: Hinoki Steam
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk, Afu（Hot-spring innkeeper Afu around fifty, salt-and-pepper short beard, deep-blue yukata under a short jacket, copper key ring at the waist, warm solid smile） steps across wet blue stone into the open-air bath（An open-air bath on the mountainside, steam rising, pool rim lined with blue stone, cedar forest and night lamps in the distance） and tests the water.

A row of five washi lanterns（A row of five washi lanterns hung on stone lamp posts by the bath, bamboo frames, inn crest painted on the paper） hangs on the bath stone lamp posts; Afu lights them one by one.

Under the office corridor（The inn's office corridor, tatami and low tables, guest-account water board on the wall, paper lanterns dim yellow） eaves hang two bath-opening brass bells（Two bath-opening brass bells hung under the office eaves, tongues tied with vermilion cord, ringing softly when the bath opens）; Afu reaches out and lets them ring softly.
Afu checks whether the brass hoops of the hinoki bath tub have loosened.
Through the bath steam, Afu looks toward the cedar-forest night lamps.
The hinoki bath tub（A man-tall round hinoki bath tub, fine wood grain, brass hoops, inn family crest carved on the rim） fills with spring water; the wood grain shines in the lantern light.
Afu sits on the blue-stone rim and listens to the creek.

In the office corridor Afu opens a chalk box and writes room numbers on the guest-account water board（A lacquer-black guest-account water board with neat white chalk writing, hung on the office wall）.
Afu sketches tonight's bath open hours in a blank corner of the water board.
Afu claps chalk dust from his hands and steps back to study the water board.
A paper lantern in the corridor sways; wood-grain gleam from the hinoki bath tub sweeps Afu's profile.

In the morning office corridor, Afu greets young Xiaoyou（Young Xiaoyou: a lean girl attendant of fourteen or fifteen, vermilion hair ribbon, pale-cyan yukata, bright stubborn eyes） driving the guest carriage（A deep-red two-wheel carriage, striped cushions in the cabin, inn family crest painted on the door, a gentle shaft horse） in.
Xiaoyou stops the deep-red carriage by the corridor stone steps and straightens the striped cushions.

Afu points to three yukata wood clips（Three yukata wood clips hung on a bamboo pole in the corridor, clip heads lacquered with different color dots） on the bamboo pole, teaching Xiaoyou to read color dots and room types.
Xiaoyou crouches in the corridor, curiously touching the tatami edge.
Afu explains to Xiaoyou the signals for opening and closing the bath.
Xiaoyou looks back at the intact guest carriage, eyes full of longing.

Behind a noren on the mountain-gate town street（A machiya street under the mountain gate, wooden lattice windows and noren curtains, stone pavement wet with rain）, Ali（Ali, nearly identical in face to young Xiaoyou, dark-green hair ribbon, bold expression, a yew wood hairpin under the ear） in a dark-green hair ribbon turns to look.
Ali strides across the wet stone slabs, bold in expression.
Ali haggles with a shopkeeper; the yew wood hairpin under her ear sways slightly.
Ali carries a bamboo basket through the machiya street crowd.
In the office corridor, Xiaoyou and Ali stand side by side—one vermilion ribbon, one dark-green.
Xiaoyou hands Ali a wood clip; the two briefly lock eyes.
Ali straightens Xiaoyou's vermilion hair ribbon, then turns her face away.
They part at the stone steps, walking opposite ways.
Months later at night, Afu keeps watch alone in the corridor; the hinoki bath tub stands by the bath.
Afu looks at the guest-account water board（The same water board blurred by hot-spring steam, writing bled, lacquer blistered）; hot-spring steam has blurred the writing on the lacquer.
Afu wipes scale from the tub rim with a cloth.
Through a gap in the paper door, Afu gazes at the black cedar forest.
The hinoki bath tub quietly steams in the night mist.
In snow season, day after day Afu sweeps the bath blue stone.
Another rainy night, Afu checks the tub's brass hoops.
In peach-blossom season, Afu watches returning guests' lamps through the steam.
At midsummer noon, Afu wipes stone lamp posts heated by the sun.
Autumn leaves cover the corridor; Afu keeps watch alone until dawn.
At dawn, Afu patrols the office corridor; the guest carriage waits by the stone steps.
Afu crouches to check the carriage shaft joints.
Afu walks to the bamboo pole; those three yukata wood clips still hang in place.
A strange blue-canopy carriage（A strange blue-canopy carriage, narrower cabin, no inn crest—not the deep-red guest carriage） passes the mountain road—narrower cabin, not the deep-red guest carriage.
Afu stands on the stone steps, logging last night's spring-temperature swings.
Afu hangs yukata on the corridor bamboo pole.
At midnight spring pressure spikes; the open-air bath boils; the hinoki bath tub shakes hard.
Hot steam swallows the stone lamp posts; lantern paper wrinkles.
A sharp crack—the hinoki bath tub（The same hinoki bath tub with a crack in the wall, brass hoop loose, hot water seeping along the seam） wall bursts, brass hoop loose and leaking.
On the mountain road, a startled horse drags the guest carriage into a creek ditch.
Shafts snap, cushions soak; the guest carriage（The deep-red carriage overturned into a creek ditch, shafts snapped, cushions soaked—a wreck that can no longer be driven） becomes a wreck.
Afu lunges to the bath and steadies the cracked hinoki bath tub.
The next day, Afu stands by the bath, staring at the cracked leaking hinoki bath tub.
Afu brushes a fingertip along the tub-wall crack, face dark.
On an office wooden post Afu records the date the guest carriage overturned.
An old photo of the guest carriage still hangs on a corridor wall nail; Afu gazes a long time.
Afu takes one of the five washi lanterns from the stone lamp posts and sits alone by its faint light.
The damaged hinoki bath tub still stands by the pool; a gap shows beside the crest.
Weeks later, Afu brings wood wedges and new brass hoops and begins repairing the hinoki bath tub.
From the storehouse Afu takes a plastic toy tub（A half-man-tall plastic toy bath tub shaped like a hinoki tub, but no crest, hoops of tin） shaped like a hinoki tub but without a crest.
Afu carefully packs the crack and tightens the brass hoop.

The hinoki bath tub（The tub crack packed with new wood wedges, brass hoop retightened, crest still there, ready to hold water again） no longer leaks; the crest is clear; it can hold spring water again.
The repaired hinoki bath tub fills with hot water; Afu breathes out in relief.
A black-hood rented rickshaw（A rented black-hood rickshaw with no inn crest and no striped cushions, carrying only luggage） stops in the corridor, nothing like the long-wrecked guest carriage.

The hot-spring guild chief（A lean hot-spring guild chief in a deep-blue uniform haori and wide-brim hat, build close to Afu's, guild crest embroidered on the cuff） steps down and talks beside Afu; the two are similar in build.
The guild chief points at the rickshaw, explaining temporary guest pickup.
The rickshaw leaves; Afu alone in the corridor watches it go.

On the mountain-gate town street comes a yuzu-candy girl（A girl selling yuzu candy on the machiya street, light-brown hair ribbon, gray yukata; at a glance like young Xiaoyou, shy gaze） in a light-brown hair ribbon; at a glance she somewhat resembles young Xiaoyou.
The girl practices handing candy; Afu shakes his head—she is not Xiaoyou after all.

Years later at dusk, Afu（The same keeper after a scald: right calf bandage seeping, limping on a bamboo cane, short-jacket cuff scorched） with a seeping bandage on his right calf leans on a bamboo cane before the abandoned bathhouse（A half-collapsed abandoned bathhouse, blackened beams, cracked dry pool floor, weeds through the stone seams）.
Afu looks up at the blackened beams, gaze far away.
Those two bath-opening brass bells under the bathhouse eaves ring softly in the wind; Afu pauses to listen.
Afu lays a palm on the cold cracked pool floor, as if saying goodbye.

By day, adult Xiaoyou（Adult Xiaoyou: a steady young woman keeper in her twenties, still in vermilion hair ribbon, yukata swapped for a deep-blue short jacket） returns along the mountain road and hurries toward the abandoned bathhouse.
By the cracked pool Xiaoyou reunites with cane-leaning Afu; the two embrace.
Beside the corridor tatami, Xiaoyou holds Afu's gaunt hand.
Afu（Afu has closed his eyes in death, lying still on the corridor tatami, face peaceful, no breath left）'s breath fades; at last he closes his eyes and passes away.
Afu's deep-blue short jacket still hangs behind the office door; Xiaoyou reaches out and gently strokes it.
By the inn lintel, adult Xiaoyou stands before the keeper's brass plaque（A brass plaque nailed to the inn lintel, engraved with Afu's name and year, edges verdigrised）.
Xiaoyou's fingertips brush Afu's name engraved on the brass plaque.
Adult Ali（Adult Ali still in dark-green hair ribbon and yew wood hairpin under the ear, expression deeper） comes from the machiya street and locks eyes with Xiaoyou at the abandoned bathhouse.
Xiaoyou and Ali stand side by side by the cracked pool—one calm-eyed, one deep in expression.
They look at each other without words, at faces alike yet different.
The shot returns to years ago—the youth straightening striped cushions in the corridor appears again.
The opening moment returns—by the bath, a round wooden tub carved with a crest fills with hot water for the first time.
Flash back to that year's machiya street—a figure in a dark-green hair ribbon with a yew wood hairpin under the ear flashes by.
Before the eyes again: that row of five old washi lanterns on the bath stone lamp posts.
Back to the dim yellow paper-lantern corridor of first meeting; the tatami is cool, as it always was.
Xiaoyou wipes that steam-blurred guest-account water board again and walks into the office corridor.
By the corridor bamboo pole, those three yukata wood clips still hang in place.
Xiaoyou takes over the hinoki bath tub; hot water fills the rim again.
